deploy.description: Readwise Reader 'Document Tags Updated' -> when a document is tagged `sendtonotion`, create an 'Article Share' idea in the Notion Social Content data source. Deduped through a free Zapier Table (Reader document id -> Notion page id) so a document is only ever turned into a page once. Migrated from the classic multi-step Zap of the same name (paused since 2026-08-29).

trigger.trigger_note: Readwise Reader 'Document Tags Updated' — a polling (read) trigger with NO input fields; it fires on any tag change to any document, so the `sendtonotion` gate lives in workflow.ts. authentication_id is the Readwise Reader connection (d.chiuten@icloud.com).
trigger.polling_dedup_caveat: Known open Zapier bug W6ZE93-VMEWP: the durable runtime dedupes trigger deliveries on the record id, so this trigger fires ONCE per Reader document, ever. Reader auto-tags articles on save, which usually uses up that firing, so a `sendtonotion` tag added later is dropped. 5 of 9 documents tagged 2026-09-16..29 were missed. No automated backstop: a scheduled sweep would need a Readwise access token (Zapier's relay won't attach the Reader connection's credentials, because the Readwise app declares no domain filter) and Dennis chose not to store one (2026-10-01). Missed tags are backfilled by hand; see the README.
trigger.catch_hook_probe_2026_10_01: Tried and reverted (PR #207 -> revert). A raw WebHookCLIAPI catch hook does NOT escape the bug: two identical POSTs carrying top-level `id: dedupe-probe-20261001` produced one run (the second was accepted with `status: success` and never ran), while a control with a different id ran within seconds. The durable dedupe keys catch-hook payloads on their top-level `id`, and Readwise puts the document id there. The native trigger was restored because it is simpler and no worse.
